title: The audio processor signalling handover every second
note: Measured in the test kernel: 'Handover signaled, but it already happened' once a second from 11 s after boot (54 by 65 s), with or without audio. Also seen in a stock boot's crash memory. Likely an interrupt wired to the wrong signal of the audio processor; compare its interrupt mapping with the Android kernel.

title: Ask each camera slot what it is
note: The first step of the cameras: a test device tree that only powers a slot (supplies, clock, reset), booted once as the second entry; then the chip's identity register read over its control bus. Turns reported sensor models into facts.

title: Image sensors: described, then identified, then seen
note: Known (research/cameras.md): the pipeline and all three control buses are bound; no sensor is described, which alone is why the cameras are dark. The vendor's kernel gives the wiring of seven sensor slots - bus, lanes, supplies, pins, clock - and names no model. Next: power one slot at a time in a test device tree and ask the chip for its identity; describe fully what this kernel already has a driver for; a frame.

title: Sound recorded through the microphone
note: Two tries on 2026-11-11 in the test kernel. The Android route sets cleanly (TX DEC0 MUX=SWR_MIC, TX SMIC MUX0=ADC0, TX_AIF1_CAP Mixer DEC0, ADC1_MIXER, ADC1, MultiMedia2 Mixer TX_CODEC_DMA_TX_3) and the card's routing wires mic bias to AMIC1-3. Starting the capture stream fails: the TX SoundWire bus can no longer read from the codec (read underflow at DPN_PortCtrl of port 1; 'Program transport params failed'), so no recording is made. Not power management: the same with the bus, macros and codec kept awake. Next lead: the moment of failure is when the bus is reshaped for the stream - compare the TX controller's frame and port parameters with the phone's Android kernel. Compared with the Android kernel: the TX bus's port layout and timings match (ports 2-5 as on sm8250 mainline and the vendor), so not the port table. The first read of a port register (DP1 PortCtrl) at stream prepare fails while hundreds of codec register accesses worked at init. Next: trace the bus's transfers (dynamic debug on the SoundWire bus and the qcom controller, or a kernel with SoundWire debugfs - this one has none).

title: The microphone codec times out at initialisation
note: Solved 2026-11-11: the audio pin driver muxed gpio19 (TX SoundWire data) to function 1 and gpio23 (RX data) to 3, where the phone's own Android kernel has 3 and 2. With both corrected the TX bus no longer clashes, the codec initialises and the sound card is made with the codec on it. The clocks going to 0 were a consequence, not the cause.

title: The modem stays in shutting-down and will not go online
note: Read the installed tqftpserv's version and source, and whether it handles rsize and seek (pmaports !4747); see what the readwrite directory holds; then one try with a fixed tqftpserv. No calls, messages or data without the author's word.

title: A SIM card in the phone
note: Inserted by the author on 2026-11-11: the card is seen (1&1, present and ready).

title: Boots that come up without the sound card
note: On 2026-11-11 one stock boot had no phone sound card: the audio processor ran with no crash, but its service channel (APR) never appeared, so no audio driver loaded. A reboot restored it. Next: a run of reboots to measure how often.

title: Port the pin fix to the microphone kernel branch
note: The tested tree came from the phone's v7.1-rc3 source plus upstream's WIP; linux-phone-oco/linux's microphone branch has the audio pin driver laid out differently (no LPI_PINGROUP entries for pins 18-23 in that form). Port the fix deliberately, rebuild from the branch, boot it, and only then add it to pull request #1.

title: Are the sensors broken, or masked by us?
note: The wiki reports the sensors working; our checks say broken. We masked hexagonrpcd-adsp-sensorspd for the suspend crash. One try: unmask it, check the sensors, then suspend once to see whether the crash returns - and record which we keep.

title: Sensors, without crashing the audio processor
note: No motion or light sensor is exposed: the sensor hub's service is masked because with it the audio processor crashed at every suspend. Sensors return when that crash is understood.
